articleTitle: Technical implications of the 1992 EEC Directive for EMC
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Interference and Design for EMC in Microprocessor Based Systems
abstract: The author summarises the requirements of the new approach (article 100) EMC Directive No. 89/336/EEC, and examines some of its implications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EMC and interference control in a microprocessor based synchronous transmission multiplexer
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Interference and Design for EMC in Microprocessor Based Systems
abstract: The authors describe how electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) was designed into a sophisticated microprocessor-controlled synchronous transmission multiplexer and how, even after meeting radiated emission and susceptibility standards, internal interference problems associated with the microprocessor can still occur. They describe the type of digital transmission equipment involved and the steps taken to make it compliant with the relevant standards, and conclude that good software design is just as important as good hardware design in achieving a product capable of satisfying EMC and interference specifications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A CAD package for the prediction and reduction of radio-frequency interference from microprocessor based electronic equipment
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Interference and Design for EMC in Microprocessor Based Systems
abstract: The authors describe the production of an EMC CAD package for use in the design of electronic computing equipment. The design of electronic equipment is split up into several separate areas such as circuit design, circuit layout, enclosure design, and thermal design. EMC considerations are taken into account at all stages in the design process.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improving the mains transient immunity of microprocessor equipment
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Interference and Design for EMC in Microprocessor Based Systems
abstract: The author looks at the sources of mains interference and explains corruption mechanisms with the help of a high-frequency equivalent circuit of a typical piece of mains powered equipment in a metal case with an interface to external equipment. He also describes retro-fit solutions such as fitting filters at the external interfaces, design guidelines worth considering when embarking on a new design and testing for mains interference immunity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design for effective EMC in microprocessor based systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Interference and Design for EMC in Microprocessor Based Systems
abstract: The failure modes of a microprocessor based system experiencing an EMC susceptibility include the possibility of a system crash, requiring a reset in order to restore normal operation. This mode of failure could have serious consequences if the system is employed in a safety critical application, such as anti-lock brakes on a motor vehicle. The failure modes are one characteristic of microprocessor based systems which warrant special consideration when designing for EMC. Another is the ability to use software techniques to detect and correct corruptions in data. These special characteristics are considered along with design techniques for good EMC performance, in terms of both emissions and immunity, which are applicable to a wider variety of circuits and systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Interference and Design for EMC in Microprocessor Based Systems
abstract: The author considers some important aspects of the power filter and examines important design criteria in the application of a filter to a device requiring protection. He also examines in more detail input current requirements and spike handling capability (transient performance) which are considered to be extremely important to the successful application of a filter. Method for improving transient response performance of a filter are also described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Interference and Design for EMC in Microprocessor Based Systems
abstract: Within the EEC, from 1992, all electrical products are to comply with the EMC Directive. This means that all electrical products have to be seen to have met the minimum relevant standard of interference-free performance. The author attempts to familiarise a manufacturer with the technical, contractual and general details an EMC test house needs to know before it can evaluate a product in a representative and cost-effective manner.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: How much screening is needed for digital systems?
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Interference and Design for EMC in Microprocessor Based Systems
abstract: The author outlines the disturbing sources and shows how the mains disturbance can couple to the victim systems. He also describes the sub-circuit sensitivity of victim systems and their electromagnetic susceptibility. He concludes with some details of equipment screening requirements necessary to achieve electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) in digital communication systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
